title: Solvable Quantum Circuits with non-Markovian Influence Matrices
authors: Samuel H. Pickering, Max McGinley, Bhavik Kumar, Bruno Bertini
abstract: Influence matrices encode the action exerted on local subsystems by the rest of an extended quantum many-body system during their evolution. Thus, knowledge of the influence matrix facilitates computationally efficient simulations of local dynamics. Here we propose a new systematic approach to generating quantum circuits with complex dynamics for which the influence matrices can be written down exactly. In contrast to previous frameworks of this kind, such as dual-unitary circuits, the resulting influence matrices are non-Markovian, exhibiting nontrivial temporal correlations. We explicitly construct a broad family of circuits of this kind, based on dressing free-fermion (matchgate) circuits with appropriately chosen interaction terms. We show that, contrary to previous solvable instances, these circuits produce patterns of correlations that closely resemble that of typical many-body systems. Our approach can be directly interpreted in terms of an error correction scheme where the terms breaking the solvability of the influence matrices play the role of errors.
summary: The paper introduces a systematic method to design solvable quantum circuits whose evolution captures non-Markovian correlations typical of interacting many-body systems. By deforming free-fermionic Clifford gates, the authors generate influence matrices that are computationally tractable while exhibiting complex temporal dependencies. This advances the field by bridging the gap between simple solvable models and realistic, strongly correlated dynamics.
main_problem: The authors aim to develop a systematic method for constructing quantum circuits whose influence matrices can be exactly calculated, specifically achieving non-Markovian dynamics while maintaining solvability.
main_result: They successfully construct a broad family of solvable circuits by deforming free-fermionic Clifford gates with interaction terms, yielding non-Markovian influence matrices that mimic complex many-body correlations.
method: The analysis involves using tensor network representations for influence matrices and applying operator trajectory decomposition in the Heisenberg picture to derive necessary structural conditions (CDU2/CDU3) for solvability.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum circuit acting on local subsystems of an extended quantum many-body system, described by $q$-level qudits arranged in a 1D array. The evolution is governed by gates derived from free-fermionic Clifford circuits.
key_observables: Influence matrices ($\mathcal{L}_t, \mathcal{R}_t$), two-point correlation function $C(x, y, t)$, and the satisfaction of structural conditions like CDU2 and CDU3.
important_parameters: The bond dimension $\chi$, fermion velocities ($v$), and interaction strengths ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that solvability can be maintained by finding specific structural deformations (e.g., restricting hopping patterns or ensuring stabilizer commutation relations) despite the introduction of non-Markovian terms.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the tensor network structure for dynamical correlations, while Figure 2 compares correlation functions for three example circuits (I, II, III) demonstrating different solvability classes (CDU2 vs CDU3).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the need for non-Markovian solvable models beyond simple dual-unitary circuits. It then details using free-fermionic Clifford gates and systematically introduces deformations ($U_I(	heta)$) to satisfy increasingly complex solvability conditions (CDU2 $	o$ CDU3), culminating in deriving local commutation relations required for full solvability.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical tool to simulate complex, non-Markovian dynamics in quantum many-body systems using structured circuits, which is highly relevant for understanding open quantum systems and realistic quantum simulation architectures.
